items.title: The Firmware Island
items.stakes: Tahvara reports nothing, in green. A whole region has missed every update for fourteen months.
items.clock: Before Thursday's bilingual board meeting in Tahvara.
items.reward: An estate where the next island shows up the day it forms.

items.sub: Tuesday · 11:40 p.m. Harrowmere · Wednesday 12:40 p.m. Tahvara

items.alt: The Harrowmere operations centre late at night, a wall of status tiles; three clocks read 23:40, 05:40 and 12:40. Yuki points at the wall; Maya, just arrived, coat still on.

bubbles.text: Harrowmere, Valmera: current. Tahvara: one hundred percent. Of nothing.
Show me what ring three actually targets.

items.caption: Wednesday lunchtime in Tahvara. Nearly midnight here.

lines.text: Ring three: zero targeted, zero failed. Every month for two years.
Zero of zero. And it's been green the whole time.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #63 · AVERY'S LENS  Zero of zero isn't success  A report must show what it didn't look at. ‘0 failed’ means nothing until you know how many were tried.  The firmware dashboard said 100% — of targeted devices. Tahvara's ring targeted none, and nobody could tell from the screen.

items.alt: A rollout sheet: ring 3 selects region = TAHV; the inventory tags Tahvara's 154 devices region = THV; the result box reads ‘targeted 0 · failed 0 · 100%’; firmware on the devices is 7.1, fourteen months old; exposure 46,200 device-days.
items.caption: A hundred percent of zero.

items.prompt: 23:50. Tahvara shows 100% with nothing behind it. What do you check first?
items.risk: A whole region without security fixes, invisible.
timeout: Yuki's shift ends; the handover says ‘Tahvara green’.
The island stays under the water line.

hints.text: 100% of what? Count the devices, not the percentages.

Ask the rollout tool how many devices ring 3 targets, query the inventory for Tahvara, and read the firmware from a sample of the devices themselves
options.result: Ring 3: zero. Inventory: 154, tagged THV. Devices: 7.1.
options.consequence: Denominator, inventory, devices — three sources that agree.

options.label: Push the latest firmware to every Tahvara device tonight
options.result: You don't yet know why they stopped updating.

items.title: Zero of zero.
items.body: Ring 3 selects devices where region = TAHV. Two years ago the asset inventory renamed Tahvara's tag to THV. Since then the ring has matched nothing, the rollout tool has reported ‘0 targeted, 0 failed’, and the dashboard has averaged over zero devices. 154 devices — a hundred and fifty-four behind a security fix published 300 days ago.
items.label: Test: how much exposure — and what should the dashboard have shown?

items.sub: Advanced · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Mara and Maya beside a board. A hundred and fifty-four devices, behind on a fix published three hundred days ago. How do I put that to the board? As exposure: devices times days. A hundred and fifty-four times three hundred — forty-six thousand two hundred device-days. And every day we argue about the rollout adds a hundred and fifty-four more. Good. Now I can argue.

items.label: **Find it:** where did Tahvara fall off?

items.title: The worm of 1988
items.body: In November 1988 a self-copying program spread across the young internet by exploiting weaknesses in widely used network services — some of them already known. Within a day it had slowed or stopped a significant share of the connected machines — by one widely quoted estimate, about one in ten — and administrators spent days cleaning up. One lesson stuck: a fix that exists but isn't installed protects nobody. A coordination centre for computer emergencies was set up within weeks.

items.text: Act II — “The pause nobody wrote down”

items.alt: Morning in Harrowmere: Maya on a video call; Sam, now running the Tahvara partner desk, on the screen.

bubbles.text: Because 7.2 silenced the interpretation channel. We paused. We told HQ. Nobody answered.

items.prompt: We stopped the updates. The Valmeran and Tahvaran channels went silent in the boardroom after 7.2. What was I supposed to do — let the board meet in silence?

options.label: “You were right to stop. What was missing was the record — a reason, an owner and a date. Let's write it now and end it properly.”
options.reply: That's… not what I expected from HQ. Okay.

options.label: “You should have asked HQ first.”
options.reply: I emailed. Twice. The mailbox belonged to someone who'd left.

options.label: “Is the routing bug fixed in 7.6?”
options.reply: Is it? Nobody told us. Test it in one room with us and we'll know.

items.title: THV
items.body: The asset team's change record from two years ago: ‘Rename region tags to three-letter codes (TAHV → THV). Impact: none expected.’ Nobody on the list owned the update rings.

items.title: The pause nobody wrote down.
items.body: Fourteen months ago release 7.2 silenced the interpretation channel in Tahvara's bilingual rooms. Sam's desk paused updates — the right call — and emailed a mailbox whose owner had left. No record, no owner at HQ, no end date. The routing bug was fixed in 7.4, nine months ago; nobody told Tahvara. Then the rename hid the island completely.
items.label: Test: what made a good pause into an island — and what does a careful rollout cost?

items.prompt: Wednesday. Mara wants all 154 updated tonight. Sam wants the interpretation channel tested first. What do you propose?
items.happening: 154 devices behind; the pause had a reason.
items.risk: A silent board meeting — or months more exposure.
timeout: The argument runs past midnight in Tahvara.
Nothing is updated; the exposure grows by 154 device-days.

hints.text: Who decides the risk, and what must the first room prove?

options.label: Push all 154 tonight
options.result: Thursday's bilingual board meeting runs on firmware nobody has tested with interpretation.
options.consequence: Fast, and blind to the reason they stopped.
options.fail: Test the thing that broke last time.

options.label: Tonight: one bilingual room with Sam's interpretation test. Friday: one site. Next Wednesday: the region. Give Mara the exposure — at most 1,078 more device-days — and let her decide, with management access restricted meanwhile
options.result: Mara approves; the pilot passes; the region is current in seven days.

options.label: Leave the island until next year's budget
options.result: Exposure keeps adding 154 device-days every day.
options.consequence: Accepting risk that isn't yours to accept.

options.label: Update only the control processors
options.result: The codecs and DSPs stay on 7.1.

items.alt: The rollout sheet after the fix: ring 3 built from the inventory list; targeted 154, updated 154, failed 0; devices in no ring: 0; pilot room → site → region with the interpretation test passed.
items.caption: Every device in a ring. The denominator on the screen.

items.title: ‘pausing updates’
items.body: Two emails from Sam's desk, fourteen months old, to firmware-hq@ — a mailbox whose owner had left the company. ‘Pausing Tahvara updates until the interpretation routing bug is fixed. Please confirm.’ Nobody did.

items.prompt: Next week. How does the next island get caught?
known: ◉ The ring depended on a free-text tag
timeout: The week fills with other work.
Ring 3 is patched; nothing else changes.

hints.text: What would have made this island visible on its first day?

options.label: Fix the tag in ring 3
options.result: The next rename breaks it again.
options.consequence: A patch for this island only.

options.label: Rings are built from the inventory's device lists; the dashboard shows targeted counts and ‘devices in no ring’; every pause is an exception with an owner, a reason and an end date
options.result: Two weeks later the dashboard flags six new Valmera cameras in no ring — the day they're installed.

options.label: Ban tag renames
options.result: The asset team's next reorganisation stalls.

options.label: A manual audit every quarter
options.result: The next island lasts up to three months.
options.consequence: Slow sampling of a fast problem.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Ask every report “of how many?”. A ring that matches nothing reports success. Exposure = devices × days at risk: it lets security weigh the cost of waiting against the cost of a hurried rollout — and the decision is theirs. A pause can be right; unrecorded, it becomes an island. Test the thing that broke last time first.
